issues.reason: "is composed of" is a stative constitution predicate that neither creates, destroys, consumes nor physically changes the molecule, and the object test is explicit — "direct object → Patient only when the action creates / destroys / consumes / physically changes it, otherwise Theme", with "when the test is unclear, default to Theme".

gaps_confirmed: constitutive "N of <mass>" NP ("molecule of water") — the of-phrase inventory (possessive, partitive "of the", measure, about-phrase) excludes the measure/constitution case without saying what replaces it; nothing licenses re-ordering it into the compound kind water_molecule
"be composed of / consist of / be made up of" — the of-complement is not a by-phrase, so the passive rule does not fix the constituents' role

per-member distribution of a counted plural inside a universal rule (each of the two hydrogen atoms attached to the oxygen atom) — Cardinality mandates an added per-member Implication, but there is no form for nesting an Implication in a rule's consequent
new_gaps: constitution has no STATIC head: PartOf is defined for a component of an object or a member of a group, so a stative "X is composed of Y" must be routed through a reified event even though no eventuality is reported — the carve-out LocatedIn makes for stative locatives has no constitution counterpart
repair_summary: Changed (Patient (sk_compose $x) $x) to (Theme (sk_compose $x) $x) in the rule consequent; every other atom, symbol and TV is unchanged.
notes: The Agent on the hydrogen group survives the object test's companion rule ("a stative transitive still takes Agent"), so only the object role needed correcting. The improvised water_molecule fusion and the reduced-relative expansion of "attached to" are gap-territory improvisations whose atoms are all true and well-typed.
